papers.summary: S-SALAAD jointly learns model weights, low-rank components, and structured sparsity during training. Its low-rank-only ablation reports a better quality–compressibility trade-off than the tested direct nuclear-norm regularization baselines.
papers.relevance: The closest match to training a model for low-rank compressibility while retaining quality.

evidence.quote: jointly learns the model weights and their low-rank and structured sparse components during training
L L -only S-SALAAD maintains low perplexity over the same budget range, providing a better trade-off between model quality and elastic compressibility than these direct regularization baselines.

papers.title: Learning Structured Sparsity for Large Models: Bridging Model Compressibility and Efficient Inference

papers.summary: BMuon changes Muon’s spectral geometry with a global MLP-channel budget and reports greater robustness to channel pruning in vision models and a 1B-parameter language model. The authors note a possible dense-model quality trade-off.
papers.relevance: Tests whether optimizer geometry can improve structured compressibility during training.

evidence.quote: Across vision and language models, BMuon is substantially more robust than Muon to magnitude-based MLP-channel pruning.
BMuon can trade dense-model quality for greater pruning robustness, as observed in our language-model experiments

papers.title: BMuon: Budgeting Muon's Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility

papers.summary: Spectrally Targeted Muon isolates which momentum singular directions are amplified. In NanoGPT, amplifying all but the few largest directions nearly matches Muon’s loss, while effective-rank measurements show that parameter spectra and loss need not move together.
papers.relevance: Direct evidence on singular spectra, effective rank, and spectral-update mechanisms in language-model training.

evidence.quote: Orthogonalizing everything except the few largest singular values of each matrix gets within 0.03 of Muon while orthogonalizing only about 13% of the momentum matrix’s magnitude
Note that structure and performance don’t move together: AdamW collapses rank and still performs well, the bottom targeted variants keep Muon’s rank without matching its loss

papers.title: Spectrally Targeted Muon

papers.summary: A theoretical comparison of singular-mode birth, saturation, and decay under several optimizers. Matrix-factorization and linear-regression experiments find substantially different transient rank dynamics even when final losses and spectra are similar.
papers.relevance: Helps distinguish optimizer-induced spectral dynamics from improved final compressibility.

evidence.quote: Under explicit balance and alignment assumptions, we derive birth, saturation, and decay laws for Euclidean GD, coordinate-wise updates of SignGD and an instantaneous Adam approximation, spectral updates of Muon and cumulative Shampoo, and a block curvature model of K-FAC.
All methods reach comparable final loss and final spectra of W W despite substantially different transient dynamics shown by the stable rank and effective rank throughout training.

papers.title: Optimizer Geometry Sets the Pace: Spectral Learning Dynamics in Matrix Factorization

papers.summary: Develops bottleneck-rank bounds for trace-norm-regularized adaptation with frozen features and a rank-deficiency result for perturbed, weight-decayed factorized LoRA. The latter is explicitly not a no-spurious-local-minima theorem.
papers.relevance: Addresses when low-rank LoRA solutions can suffice and how regularization shapes them.

evidence.quote: we prove that the trace-norm-regularized problem has a global minimizer whose rank is controlled by d Φ
This is a first-order exclusion theorem, not a no-spurious-local-minima theorem

papers.title: How Finite-Rank Bottlenecks Shape the Low-Rank Adaptation Landscape

papers.summary: A module-matched LoRA rank sweep under label noise compares adapters with dense fine-tuning of the same modules. In the reported 7B text-classification experiment, every sampled rank, including parameter parity, has higher test negative log-likelihood than dense fine-tuning across three paired seeds.
papers.relevance: Directly connects adapter rank, noisy-label memorization, and generalization using a controlled dense reference.

evidence.quote: Every sampled rank, parity included, remains behind dense in all three seeds
The dense arm trains the weights of those projections and freezes their biases, as does LoRA. Both arms train the same classification head with the same optimizer settings.

papers.title: LoRA's Second Descent Extends Beyond Parameter Parity

papers.summary: Ori tracks drifting gradient subspaces for low-rank LLM training. Across fixed-token-budget LLaMA experiments, it reports gains over GaLore under tight rank constraints; the reported memory figures measure the optimizer step, not total peak training memory.
papers.relevance: A direct GaLore-related comparison of low-rank training quality, rank, and optimizer memory.

evidence.quote: when training the 130M model at an aggressively low rank of just 16, Ori achieves a validation perplexity of 43.61, substantially outperforming GaLore (60.29) and OSD (54.05)
Our goal is to record the peak memory usage, incurred solely by the said optimizer’s update step.

papers.title: Ori: Drift-Aware Streaming $k$-PCA for Very Low-Rank LLM Training

papers.summary: Monarch–Muon combines structured weight factors with Muon. At a 6.89B dense-reference size, its single-H100 systems measurements report 52.94 versus 68.87 GB peak allocated memory and 1638.6 versus 2986.9 ms full-step time relative to dense Muon; quality comparisons are reported separately at smaller scales.
papers.relevance: Measures how structured parameterization affects weights, gradients, optimizer state, and training time as scale changes.

evidence.quote: Table 2 : Training costs on one H100 at microbatch 4, indexed by the dense reference model size. Monarch–Muon uses 4 blocks.
At 6.89B, Monarch–Muon reduces the full-step time by 45% and peak memory by 23% relative to dense Muon.

papers.title: Monarch-Muon: Structure-Aware Muon for Fast and Memory-Efficient Pretraining

papers.summary: ResQAdam retains a BF16 momentum, applies Adam in a principal low-rank subspace, and uses the residual’s sign. In the reported QAT measurements across three LLMs, optimizer-state memory falls by 71–74%, total peak memory by 15.3–19.5%, and throughput by less than 2% relative to AdamW.
papers.relevance: A concrete quality–memory–throughput study of low-rank optimizer-state compression, specifically for quantization-aware training.

evidence.quote: It keeps a single BF16 momentum, applies Adam only to the r × r r\times r coordinates of the principal subspace, and adds a normalized sign update computed from the residual.

This efficiency directly translates to a 15.3% to 19.5% reduction in total peak memory. This substantial memory reduction incurs minimal computational overhead. The training throughput decreases by less than 2% compared to standard AdamW in all evaluated cases.

papers.title: ResQAdam: Residual-Preserving Adaptive Optimization for Memory-Efficient Quantization Aware Training

papers.summary: CORE is a training-free deep-research harness that retrieves broad passages but returns selected snippets, with context expansion and duplicate suppression. In its controlled closed-search comparisons, it reports higher answer accuracy and evidence recall than the two evaluated harnesses.
papers.relevance: Directly informs retrieval and context-management choices for a handwritten research-digest agent, although its benchmarks are not digest curation.

evidence.quote: CORE’s context manager lets the agent expand the context around previously retrieved sources and deduplicates snippets across searches.
Across three agent models and three benchmarks, CORE achieves higher answer accuracy and evidence recall than Tongyi DeepResearch and OpenResearcher in every model–benchmark comparison

papers.title: CORE: Coarse-to-Fine Search with Context Management for Deep Research

BMuon studies structured channel pruning rather than low-rank factorization and reports a dense-quality trade-off. ResQAdam’s evaluated setting is QAT.
CORE was evaluated on deep-research question answering, not research-digest selection. X analysis was disabled.
